text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Smart-routing observed repetitive fallback loop for requests hitting /v1/chat in eu-west-1. Error spike starting ~10:02 UTC, 5xx rate up x6. Automatic mitigation attempted but loop persisted. Paging oncall.

oncall-matt: Acked. I’m on it. Paging SREs and infra. :eyes:

diego: I see a pattern in the routing logs — the smart-router is selecting a quantized variant (q8_0) for a model that only supports fp16 tool-calling. The quant variant returns a capability error so routing bounces to region fallback, which then re-routes back and re-selects the quant variant => loop.

sara: Can you paste the relevant log snippet? I want to confirm error type before we flip anything.

diego: sure, logs:

```
2026-03-15T10:02:11Z router[smart-route]: request id=abc123 route=eu-west-1 -> model=redwood-alpha-q8_0 variant=quantized
2026-03-15T10:02:11Z serve[variant-check]: variant.capabilities.tool_calling=false
2026-03-15T10:02:12Z model-client: error=ToolCallNotSupported: requested tool_calling-only input
2026-03-15T10:02:12Z router[smart-route]: fallback -> region=us-west-2 policy=latency-pref
2026-03-15T10:02:12Z router[smart-route]: region=us-west-2 -> model=redwood-alpha-q8_0 (same variant set chosen)
```

This explains the loop. The compatibility matrix currently marks q8_0 as compatible for redwood-alpha in eu region (false positive).

elaine: Does the failed request surface to customers as 5xx or is it hidden by retries? CS, any reports?

customer-success-ash: Getting several customer messages about slow/unavailable chat responses from EU tenants. Severity: multiple mid-market customers. Two have reported timeouts in the last 10m. We're escalating to them that we're investigating.

product-lead-kim: Quick ask — any customer-visible data loss or incorrect outputs? We should prepare a status note.

diego: So far it's timeouts and increased latency; requests are retried to other regions and sometimes succeed, sometimes error. No known incorrect content returned — just failure to execute tool calls when client expected that capability.

infra-jen: Proposed mitigations:
1) disable quantized variant selection for redwood-alpha in eu-west-1 routing pool (hot patch to routing policy)
2) mark q8_0 as "no-tool-call" in compatibility matrix to prevent future selection
3) force sticky region preference for customers currently failing to avoid oscillation
4) monitor for downstream cost increases

I can push #1 and #3 as a quick mitigation. #2 requires a config change in model-compat service and a small rollout.

oncall-matt: Do #1 + #3 now. Dieogo (diego) + jen coordinate for #2.

deploy-bot: Runbook step: `rwctl routing update --pool eu-west-1 --model redwood-alpha --disable-variant q8_0` queued by infra-jen

infra-jen: Executing now.

```
$ rwctl routing patch --pool eu-west-1 --model redwood-alpha --remove-variant q8_0
PATCH /routing/pools/eu-west-1/models/redwood-alpha 200 OK
```

infra-jen: Variant disabled. Observability: 5xx rate starting to fall in eu-west-1, retries decreasing. Latency trending down.

diego: I’ve started a compatibility-matrix patch to mark q8_0 as incompatible for tool_calling on redwood-alpha. That requires a deploy of model-compat service (canary first).

```
# compat update snippet
compat.patch:
- model: redwood-alpha
  variant: q8_0
  capabilities:
    tool_calling: false
```

sara: Can you also add context-length metadata? We noticed some variants have truncated kv cache sizes which can cause silent failures for long contexts.

diego: Good catch — adding context_length_max: 2048 for quant variants in eu. Will include in the same patch.

product-lead-kim: CS: please send a brief to the customers impacted that we're mitigating and expected recovery ~10-15 minutes after patch.

customer-success-ash: On it, sending customers a short note. Will post follow-up in thread with customer IDs.

oncall-matt: Monitoring: KPI checks show recovery at +8m after patch. We should keep quant variants disabled in eu until matrix patch is live and we do a canary.

elaine: Agreed. Also file a follow-up postmortem and label as severity P2 (service degradation for multiple customers). We need root cause: bad entry in compatibility matrix + routing policy that ranks variant capacity before capability.

diego: Root cause summary draft: an automated model onboarding job incorrectly inferred tool_calling capability for q8_0 based on model name heuristics. Routing policy ranked lowest-cost variant, ignoring capability predicate in rare tie-break conditions. Fixes: tighten onboarding heuristics, add explicit capability checks in routing decision path, and add a unit test for tool_calling capability enforcement.

infra-jen: I'll open the PRs for the routing check and post a canary plan for the matrix change (20% traffic eu-west canary for 15m). Need approvals from product and eng-ml.

product-lead-kim: Approve canary. Notify legal/compliance if any customers in regulated industries were impacted (Ash?)

customer-success-ash: Two customers are in fintech in EU — CS will coordinate with legal if needed.

oncall-matt: Action items recap:
- infra-jen: hot patch routing (done)
- diego: compat-matrix patch + canary (in progress)
- sara: add context-length metadata + test cases (in progress)
- ash: customer comms (in progress)
- kim: status update for execs

deploy-bot: `deploy canary model-compat v2026.03.15-canary` started by diego

diego: Canary running for 20% traffic in eu-west-1. No regressions in 10m. Will ramp to 100% in 15m if stable.

infra-jen: Observability: 5xxs down to baseline, tail latency normalized. Customers reporting improved response.

customer-success-ash: Customers updated, one fintech customer replied that things look normal again. They appreciate the quick fix.

oncall-matt: Leaving this in monitoring state. Will run postmortem tomorrow EOD. If anything regresses, page me immediately. Great job team. :thumbsup:

elaine: Please include the automation runbook step to prevent automatic variant selection until matrix is verified. Also add a metric alert for variant-capability-mismatch count > 1/min.

sara: I'll add the alert rule and the runbook note.

product-lead-kim: Postmortem priority: must include timeline, customer impact table, mitigation steps, and proposed changes to onboarding heuristics. Assigning to diego + sara.

diego: Will draft postmortem. Adding links to logs + routing decision traces in the doc.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: fallbacks normalized, quant variant disabled in eu pool until matrix fix completes. Severity downgraded to P2 — follow-up postmortem scheduled.

oncall-matt: Thread close when postmortem link is posted. Thanks all.
__note: This document is a single Slack thread; messages are in chronological order and are presented as a continuous string prefixed by sender display name.
